title: Recursive shelves: First qualifying slip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Recursively inspect half-open ranges [left,right), starting with the whole array. For each nonempty range, record its sum, then inspect its left half and right half using mid=floor((left+right)/2); stop splitting a one-element range. Produce the recorded sums in that preorder. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A shelf audit divides each occupied range in half and records its subtotal before opening smaller ranges. Luz needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

unitIntro: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Recursively inspect half-open ranges [left,right), starting with the whole array. For each nonempty range, record its sum, then inspect its left half and right half using mid=floor((left+right)/2); stop splitting a one-element range. Produce the recorded sums in that preorder. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with divide-and-conquer recursion. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
